title: Culpeper's Complete Herbal (fixture excerpts)
text: Wormwood. This is an Herb of Mars, and therefore not to be uſed where the ſtomack is hot and dry. The decoction of the leaves in wine is good againſt the dropſie, and expelleth choler and melancholy from the ſtomack and liver. The ſeeds kill worms in the belly. The juice mixed with honey, and the eyes anointed therewith, taketh away the dimneſs of ſight. The diſtillation of the leaves yieldeth a bitter water, good for the ſtomack. It is hot and dry in the ſecond degree, and bitter in taſte.

title: Culpeper's Complete Herbal (fixture excerpts)
text: Lungwort. The leaves of this plant are ſpotted like a lung, and it is for that reaſon called Pulmonaria. It is an Herb of Jupiter, and is much commended for the lungs. The decoction of the leaves in water is good for a cough, and for the phthiſick. The leaves ſtamped and laid to the ſore, healeth it. It is cold and dry.

title: Culpeper's Complete Herbal (fixture excerpts)
text: Saffron. It is an Herb of the Sun, and the flowre is of a yellow colour. The yellow flowre is good for the jaundice, and comforteth the heart. The decoction of the flowres in wine is given againſt the plague. It is hot and dry in the ſecond degree. A tincture of the flowres is good for the ſtomack.

title: Culpeper's Complete Herbal (fixture excerpts)
text: Comfrey. The root is knotted and joined like a bone, and therefore it is ſaid to heal bones. It is an Herb of Saturn. The decoction of the root in wine is good for broken bones, and for wounds. The root ſtamped and laid to a wound ſtayeth the bleeding. It is cold and dry, and of a clammy ſlimy ſubſtance.

title: The Herball or Generall Historie of Plantes (fixture excerpts)
text: Betony. Betony is good for the head, and for all diſeaſes thereof. It is an Herb of Mars. The decoction thereof in mead is good for the falling ſickneſs, and for the ſpleen. The powder of the leaves is good for the ſtomack. The infuſion of the leaves in wine is good for the head.

title: Culpeper's Complete Herbal (fixture excerpts)
text: Fennel. The ſeeds are hot and dry in the third degree. The infuſion of the ſeeds is good for the eyes, and taketh away the dimneſs of ſight. The diſtilled water of the ſeeds is good for the ſtomack. The root is good for the jaundice. It is an Herb of Mercury.

title: Spagyric and Tria Prima texts (fixture excerpts)
text: Of the Spagyric Art. The firſt operation is calcination, whereby the body is reduced to aſhes and calx. Then followeth diſſolution with the menſtruum, which is water, vinegar, wine, or the ſpirit of wine. After diſſolution, digeſt the matter in a gentle heat, as in the dung of horſes or the balneum, for the ſpace of a month. Then diſtill the ſpirit by gentle fire, that the volatile parts may ariſe. The reſidue is the caput mortuum. By ſpagyria we ſeparate the three principles: the ſalt, the ſulphur, and the mercury.

title: The Greek Herbal of Dioscorides (Goodyer 1655, fixture excerpts)
text: Of the Willow Tree. The leaves and bark of the willow being bruiſed and boiled in wine, and the decoction drunk, doth eaſe the pains of the back and the ſciatica. The bark ſtamped and laid on a hot ſwelling abateth the heat. It is cold and dry in the ſecond degree.

title: Culpeper's Complete Herbal (fixture excerpts)
text: Poppy. The head of the poppy is cold and dry in the fourth degree, and is an Herb of the Moon. The decoction of the heads in water cauſeth ſleep, and eaſeth pain. The ſyrup of poppies is good for a cough, and for the rheum. The ſeeds are uſed in the kitchen. It ſtayeth the flux.

title: Culpeper's Complete Herbal (fixture excerpts)
text: Garlic. Garlic is hot and dry in the fourth degree, and is an Herb of Mars. Being eaten it expelleth wind, and is good for the ſtomack. The juice is good for the cough, and for the ſhortneſs of breath. It is held to be good againſt the plague. The diſtilled water is good for the head. The ſyrup of garlic and honey is good for a cold.

title: Culpeper's Complete Herbal (fixture excerpts)
text: Mint. Mint is hot and dry in the ſecond degree, and is an Herb of Venus. The decoction of the leaves is good for the ſtomack, and ſtayeth vomiting. The juice mixed with vinegar ſtayeth the bleeding of the nose. The water of mint is good for the head. The ſyrup of mint comforteth the heart.

title: Spagyric and Tria Prima texts (fixture excerpts)
text: Of the Tria Prima. All things conſiſt of ſalt, ſulphur, and mercury. The ſalt is the body, the ſulphur the ſoul, and the mercury the ſpirit. Burn the herb to aſhes and thereby make the ſalt of the plant by lixiviation. The ſulphur is drawn out by the menſtruum, and the mercury by diſtillation. This is the ſpagyric preparation, which ſeparateth the pure from the impure.
